newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government prices rise pre weekend.
newsitem.headline: Russian government prices rise pre weekend.

text.p: Prices of Russian government paper edged up on Friday as banks, unwilling to sit on cash ahead of the weekend, put money into securities, dealers said.
Traders had mixed views of where the market was heading.
"As a rule, banks prefer not to hold cash over the weekend but to buy paper," Imperial Bank dealer Sergei Gubanov said. "Prices went up a bit."
Tokobank dealer Vadim Kononov forecast prices for one-year T-bills and OFZ bonds rising due to their high yields.
But Gubanov said prices could fall in coming days as banks seek to secure roubles ahead of big-volume auctions next Wednesday.
The domestic rouble market took a breather after two days of active trading, and dealers forecast the rouble edging up against the dollar on heavy clients demand ahead of the auctions.
Roubles with tomorrow delivery slipped to 5,776-77 on Friday from 5,775-77. Overnight credits edged up to 5-10 percent from 2-4 percent.
The Finance Ministry will offer a total of 18 trillion roubles worth of T-bills and bonds for auctions on Wednesday.
Prices for government paper have risen as newly-confident investors seek to get into the market.
